date: Sixth-century grant, renewed in the seventh century
territory: Grant district traditionally associated with the Sylhet region
reach_assessment: Authority to grant and renew land is recorded. The size and modern perimeter of the district are not established here.
duration: Earlier grant followed by renewal; continuous territorial control is not demonstrated by this alone.
boundary_limit: The map uses the Nidhanpur findspot as an orientation anchor, not the boundary of the donated land. This is administrative evidence, not a narrated conquest.

territory: Karṇasuvarṇa near modern Murshidabad, West Bengal
reach_assessment: A victory camp at Karṇasuvarṇa is directly attested. Wider control of Gauḍa is inferred by historians, with disagreement about its date, duration and extent.
duration: Duration of occupation or control is disputed.
boundary_limit: An attested camp does not supply the perimeter of an annexed province. Sircar’s discussion and Sharma’s reconstruction differ; neither permits an exact conquered-area polygon.

date: Eighth century; ruler identification and inscription dating vary
territory: Named eastern-Indian regions; three approximate regional references are mapped
reach_assessment: The Paśupati inscription calls Harshadeva lord of these regions. The identification with Kamarupa’s ruler is the historical interpretation used here; permanent provincial administration is not established.
duration: Tenure and duration of any control are not specified.
boundary_limit: This is a royal eulogy in a Nepalese inscription. It gives no surveyed borders. Kośala is retained in the list without choosing an unverified modern location. Nepal is the inscription’s location and marriage connection, not a conquest.
mapped_references: Gauḍa · claim; Oḍra · claim; Kaliṅga · claim

territory: Gauḍa; an advance to the Ganges is inferred from the victory verse
reach_assessment: Gachtal verse 15 reports defeat of Rajyapala of Gauḍa and invokes the Ganges. Sircar reads this as an advance to its bank, without defining a lasting annexation.
duration: No duration or annexed perimeter is stated.
boundary_limit: The regional anchor does not locate the battle or a precise Ganges crossing. No whole-Bengal annexation or area in km² is inferred.

reach_assessment: Gachtal verse 20 reports Indrapala defeating Kalyanachandra of Vaṅga in an encounter involving boats. It does not define land annexed after the encounter.
duration: Occupation or lasting possession is not established.
boundary_limit: The marker orients the reader within eastern Bengal; it is not a located battlefield. Defeating a ruler is not proof of acquiring all his dominions.

territory: Davaka, associated with the Kapili–Nagaon region
reach_assessment: Its absorption into the expanding kingdom is reconstructed. Kalyanavarman is often credited; other scholarship credits Balavarman.
duration: Individual king and precise date unresolved.
boundary_limit: It concerns consolidation within the later Kamarupa landscape, not a securely measured external province. Included in the ledger, not drawn as won territory.

territory: No defensible named eastern endpoint in the sources checked
reach_assessment: Choudhury attributes further eastern subjugation to Mahendravarman. That does not identify a mappable conquered district.
boundary_limit: No polygon or endpoint is supplied. Horse-sacrifice claims are not converted into a map of conquered lands.

territory: A named grant district; its modern identification and external extent are debated
reach_assessment: Grant references support royal land authority. Reconstructions of a much larger Bengal domain depend on contested place identifications.
boundary_limit: An external conquered province is not mapped from uncertain identifications.
